reasons: The termination section (4(c)) contains no transition assistance, data return/export, or deletion certification obligation, and permits unilateral destruction of the other Party's Confidential Information — this fails the fallback (90 days assistance + 30-day export) and approaches walk-away territory, so 'deviation' with an insert is correctly classified.

The inserted subparagraph (v) is appended to the existing termination list without altering p0019–p0022, tracks the model language (6-month assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return/export, certified deletion), and adapts the data reference to the Agreement's actual terms ('Requests, Content and other Customer data') since 'Customer Data' is undefined — a reasonable, minimal edit.
The backup/legal-retention carve-out on deletion is a customary, non-prejudicial qualifier and does not undermine the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change and offers the 90-day fallback while preserving the 30-day export and deletion certificate.
Deterministic checks pass and the redline is placed in the correct (termination) section as the redline guidance directs.
